name: cytoband_arms
code_version_note: the commit at build time, which precedes the commit that lands this file
method: One row per canonical contig, reduced from the band table's ~1,200 rows. The centromere is the span of the bands stained acen — there are always two, one either side of the constriction — so p_end is the first acen start and q_start is the last acen end; that is the definition of an arm boundary rather than a threshold. chrom_length is the largest band end on the contig, which is the assembly length the band table itself asserts. acrocentric is read from the file's own stain column: a chromosome carrying a stalk band on its short arm (13, 14, 15, 21, 22) has no callable p arm, and step 8 reports it q-arm-only. Alternate haplotypes and patch contigs are dropped: they have no centromere and no arms.

inputs.name: UCSC hg38 cytoBand
inputs.role: cytogenetic band intervals and stains, from which the arm boundaries come

licence: UCSC Genome Browser data are free for any use; the cytogenetic band table is derived from published ideograms and carries no restriction on redistribution.
patient_data: none. Public reference data only - a gene, a transcript, a published classification or a literature range. This manifest records URLs, releases, digests and counts.
note: 24 contigs: 22 autosomes plus X and Y. The positions here are reference geometry — where a centromere sits in GRCh38 — and say nothing about any sample, which is why the table is committed while every table derived from the child's callset is not.
